analysis:
Both units are head-side excerpts of CHANGELOG.md (lines 3159-3650), documentation-only prose. I found no code, configuration, workflow or script content in these lines, so they cannot change enforcement behavior on their own.

Security-relevant claims the changelog makes, which the next pass should check against the actual changed files, not this prose:
- Line 3160: prod signing is tag-gated and scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh refuses prod on non-tag triggers.
- Line 3165: scripts/install.sh relaxes the signature check for versions carrying -dev. or -staging., while keeping the bundle identifier pinned. This touches T-034, T-013 and TB-009 trust assumptions. Check that the version-string gate cannot be reached with a production binary or a production coordinator. Whether the relaxed installer is served only by the dev coordinator is unverified here (line 3165).
- Line 3164: a new dispatch-only dev-branch workflow, release-dev-branch.yml. Check that it has no production secrets and no production signing identity.
- Line 3166: the changelog itself says the lane has not completed a run.
- Lines 3199-3245: threat-review CI changes, including review-control, merge-clearance and spend limits. These sit outside the provider threat model's main scope, but are worth confirming in the workflow files.
- T-041 (SSD cache): changelog mentions at lines 3179-3183 and 3307-3321 describe test-fixture working-volume selection, write-budget defaults and storage validation, with production safeguards stated unchanged. The source files were not supplied, so this is not verified.

The patch excerpt is truncated, so the rest of the PR (scripts, workflows, Swift sources) is not covered by these units. No findings are raised from changelog text alone; the open questions above are about integration with other files.
